projects.title: OD Travel Time Matrix, 97 US Cities
projects.subtitle: ArcGIS Pro Network Analyst
projects.description: A large-scale origin-destination cost matrix for 97 U.S. cities in ArcGIS Pro Network Analyst, computing neighborhood-to-neighborhood travel times on a custom road network.
projects.longDescription: I built this as an Upwork freelance project in the GIS Analyst role, focused on network analysis and spatial data processing. The work covers 97 U.S. cities. I used a custom road network with pre-calculated travel-time costs and a neighborhood point layer for each city, built a Network Dataset, and ran OD Cost Matrix analysis so every neighborhood pair within a city received a travel time. The output was tens of millions of OD records, including a merged table of about 57 million rows, delivered as geodatabases, shapefiles, and Excel schema reports. A follow-up project extended and refined the original analysis. The client rated the work 5.0 out of 5.
features: OD Cost Matrix for 97 U.S. cities
Custom road network with pre-calculated travel-time costs
Neighborhood point layers per city
Network Dataset built in ArcGIS Pro
Travel time between every neighborhood pair within each city
Tens of millions of OD records, including a merged table of about 57 million rows
Deliverables: geodatabases, shapefiles, and Excel schema reports
Follow-up project to extend and refine the analysis
Client rating 5.0 out of 5

projects.title: AmeriWater Dealer Territory Map
projects.subtitle: Region-based ZIP3 viewer
projects.description: An ArcGIS web app that maps AmeriWater dealer coverage across 854 ZIP3 territories, with region filters, dealer coloring, and a full-screen map workspace.
projects.longDescription: I built this dealer territory map as an Upwork freelance project for AmeriWater. It is a full-viewport ArcGIS 4.32 app that draws real ZIP boundaries from Esri's USA Boundaries service and colors each ZIP3 by dealer. Four sales regions sit as pills at the top: Brian Bates, Dave Tholin, Tommy LoVoi, and Med Water | Bates. You can select more than one region or state, switch Primary / Secondary / Show All dealer views, and click a territory for region, ZIP, and account details, including a Strategic badge where it applies. A bottom toolbar holds layers, search, basemaps, labels, scale, and a light or liquid-glass theme. Preferences stay in the browser. Administrators can refresh the 854 ZIP3 records from a CSV and deploy an updated data file.
features: 854 ZIP3 territories on real Esri ZIP geometry
Four-region filter with multi-select pills
Primary, Secondary, and Show All dealer views
State chips combined with region filters, then auto-zoom to the result
Territory detail card with Strategic badge and dealer accounts
Search by dealer, ZIP3, or state
Gray, Streets, and Satellite basemaps
ZIP3 or dealer labels, dual-unit scale bar, and a live status bar
Light theme and liquid-glass theme, saved in the browser

projects.title: Agroptics Field Maps
projects.subtitle: Leaflet maps for satellite irrigation
projects.description: The interactive map for Agroptics: growers draw farm fields, then view Planet, Sentinel, Landsat, and WaPOR crop and water layers inside the Gulf Terminal platform.
projects.longDescription: Agroptics is Gulf Terminal's satellite irrigation platform. Growers define field boundaries, send that geometry to the backend, and then read crop and water data on the same map. My main work was the map itself. I wrote the full Leaflet front end in vanilla JavaScript, with no framework, so the same map can open in add-field, edit-field, and season-detail screens. Add and edit modes cover the field lifecycle: draw a polygon, circle, or rectangle, or upload GeoJSON, KML, KMZ, or Shapefile. You can edit vertices, split a field, delete it, catch overlaps, and keep area under a limit. Display mode is read-only. It loads satellite index rasters with a color legend, plus measure, search, geolocation, and download. The dashboard map switches Planet, Sentinel, Landsat, and WaPOR, then layers such as water demand, crop vigor, fractional cover, NDVI, MSAVI, and ETc. Behind the map, I wrote the Planet satellite processing in Python, including the AWS steps. The team converted that code to .NET for production. The map still talks to the backend through init, setFeatures, and getAllFeatures so field geometry and metadata stay with the rest of the Agroptics app.
features: Embeddable map for add, edit, and display screens
Draw polygon, circle, or rectangle field boundaries
Upload GeoJSON, KML, KMZ, or Shapefile
Edit vertices, split fields, delete, overlap checks, and an area limit
Read-only dashboards with measure, search, geolocation, and download
Planet, Sentinel, Landsat, and WaPOR sources on the season map
Satellite index overlays: water demand, crop vigor, fractional cover, NDVI, MSAVI, ETc
Category legend and date playback for index rasters
FAO WaPOR water-productivity layers in display mode
Python processing for Planet images on AWS, later converted to .NET

projects.title: COP27, Sharm El-Sheikh

projects.title: Clustering

projects.description: A learning project on FeatureReductionCluster for dense point layers in the ArcGIS API for JavaScript.
projects.longDescription: A learning project on point clustering with the ArcGIS API for JavaScript. I also built a FeatureLayer from client-side features, including the schema the API requires.

Interactive cluster exploration
